_readme: THE ONE FILE TO EDIT to wire /cost/ into the live signup form. No code change is needed.
1. formURL — the form's LONG prefill base, ending in /viewform. Get it from the form's
three-dot menu -> 'Get pre-filled link'. A forms.gle short link will NOT work: it drops
the query string, and the query string is the whole point. While formURL is empty, /cost/
shows the ordinary signup button instead of a prefilled one, so nothing ever links to a
half-wired URL.
2. entry — the digits of each question's entry.NNNN id. Run logPrefillIds() in the form's
Apps Script project, or read them out of the 'Get pre-filled link' URL, which is
authoritative. Digits only: the page writes the 'entry.' prefix itself. While any one of
the three is empty, no prefilled link is built at all — a partial prefill would silently
drop a choice the participant thought they had made.
3. label — MUST match the live form's option label BYTE FOR BYTE, em dashes and curly
apostrophes included. Google Forms matches a prefill value against the option string; a
mismatch selects nothing and the participant lands on an empty question.
SUNDAY IS A PLAIN THREE-WAY CHOICE (31 Aug 2026, Konrad: "25 vs 50 for sunday. you can just
have that as multiple choice. way simpler"). It was briefly tier-dependent — two questions on
the live form, and a priceFrom/priceField lookup in this file whose Sunday labels carried no
euro amount — and all of that is gone. The form now asks it ONCE, in a section BOTH
accommodation branches reach, with three options that each carry exactly one euro amount which
IS that option’s price. So Sunday obeys the same contract as every other question below and
the calculator reads its price off the chosen label.
PRICE LABEL CONTRACT (POLICY.md, machine contract): every priced label carries exactly one
euro amount and it is that option's price. Nothing in this file states a price as a number:
the page and qa/cost-logic.js both extract it from the label with the same regex the sheet
uses, so the site cannot drift from the form. qa/cost-logic.js fails the build if a label
carries zero or two euro amounts.
'name' is what the page shows; 'label' is what the form receives. They differ only so the
page can put the price in its own column.
